title: Cerulean Ports — integration lab notebook
content:
Context:
Cerulean Ports is testing Redwood Private on a small on-prem cluster (2xA100 equivalent, NVMe local). They want an assistant that summarizes ship manifests, highlights customs hold flags, and suggests routing optimizations. Primary concerns: latency during peak scan/batch loads, data residency, and deterministic fallbacks when the model is under load.

Meeting notes (2025-11-03 sync):
- Quick intro: Cerulean infra team (Asha, Marco) + logistics product lead (R. Kim).
- They have nightly bulk ingestion (60k manifests/day) and interactive operator queries (~600 q/hr office hours).
- Goal: sub-250ms tail latency for interactive queries 95th percentile; nightly batch can be slower but should not block DB updates.
- They want private deployment (VPC) with customer KMS and audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance.

Key technical constraints they mentioned:
- No external egress from on-prem inference host (air-gapped-ish).
- Existing infra uses Redis for short-term caches and S3-compatible object store for long-term manifests.
- Operators run prompts that frequently reference recent manifests — prefix cache hit rate needs to be high.
- Peak concurrency expected: ~80 concurrent interactive users during shift overlap.

Requirements (initial, prioritized):
1) Private deployment with KMS integration (must)
2) API endpoint accessible via their internal gateway (mTLS) (must)
3) Prefix/KV cache persisted locally across restarts for warm startup (should)
4) Observability: per-route token cost and 95th/99th latency in Console (should)
5) Canary rollout for model updates and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant (nice-to-have)
6) Nightly bulk scoring worker that can use same model artifacts but run in offline mode (nice-to-have)

Gotchas & engineering notes (from convo + quick triage):
- Disk I/O: NVMe is limited; when the KV cache grows beyond available fast storage the host falls back to remote store causing >2s spikes. Need to enforce cache size caps and eviction policy.
- Model variant mix: their preferred quality variant (fp16 70B) is heavy; fallback to 8-bit quantized 70B helps cost but sometimes changes entity extraction heuristics. We should surface regression alerts tied to prompt set.
- mTLS termination: their gateway performs mTLS and then forwards traffic to internal network; our Private control plane needs to know the client cert subject for audit mapping — confirm with security.
- Concurrent KV access: the nightly bulk job writes new manifest prefixes and can evict keys unexpectedly during operator queries. Need workload-aware batching to isolate bulk writes.

Quick test prompts (short list for early QA):
- "Summarize manifest ID M-2025-11-01-0042: list potential customs flags and reasons."
- "Show last 3 ports of call for vessel ‘FSL NEVERMORE’ and any anomalies in cargo counts."
- "If container C-214 shows mismatch weight vs declared, suggest immediate steps and expected hold time."

Performance targets (agreed as first pass):
- Interactive 95th pctl <= 250ms for text-only summaries (no heavy rerank)
- Token budget per query capped to 512 tokens (operators can request more via bulk workflow)
- Nightly bulk throughput target: 100 manifests/sec sustained for scoring window (non-blocking)

Action items (owners & tentative dates):
- Maya: deliver integration checklist + minimal KMS config sample by 2025-11-07.
- Jonas: prototype local KV eviction cap (config flag) + benchmark script by 2025-11-12.
- Priya: draft canary/fallback policy doc showing route rules and fallbacks by 2025-11-14.
- Ethan: PoC of mTLS cert subject mapping in Private control plane with Cerulean gateway sample by 2025-11-10.
- Cerulean (Asha/Marco): provide sample manifest payloads (sanitized) and access to their test VPC by 2025-11-06.

Open questions for Cerulean (need answers before next run):
- Can they allocate ~120GB NVMe to the inference host for KV + model cache? If not, what's acceptable?
- Do they want audit logs forwarded in real-time or batched (hourly)?
- Which internal DNS name will the gateway use for API calls (needed for cert)?
- Are there any regulatory retention windows for logs we should be aware of?

Integration checklist (minimal technical steps):
- Provision Private control plane with customer KMS entry + vault config.
- Deploy inference host with model artifacts (fp16 70B + quantized 8-bit variant).
- Configure KV cache path to NVMe mount; set eviction cap = 90GB (tweak after benchmark).
- Enable mTLS endpoint; coordinate cert CN mapping with Cerulean security.
- Add console dashboards: per-route latency, token breakdown, KV hit rate metric.
- Wire audit logs to Cerulean Splunk (initially as hourly batches).

Notes from quick infra experiment (11/04):
- On local A100-like VM, disabling persistent KV caused warmup time > 90s on restart; with persisted KV snapshot warmup dropped to ~12s.
- Quantized model dropped p95 latency by ~30% but produced 3% fewer entity annotations on small eval set (investigate adapter/temperature tuning).

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: insufficient NVMe -> latency spikes. Mitigation: default to small model variant for interactive route and reserve dedicated node pool for bulk scoring.
- Risk: model regression after rollout. Mitigation: gate rollouts on automated eval set (Cerulean-provided prompt set) and enable automatic rollback if quality delta > threshold.

Next sync: 2025-11-10 (engineering deep-dive). Prepare: benchmark numbers (Jonas), KMS sample (Maya), sanitized sample manifests (Cerulean).

Freeform/brain dump:
- Could use adaptive batching: increase batch size for operators whose queries are similar (same ship ID) to improve KV reuse.
- Consider a small in-memory LRU for most-recently-accessed prefixes to safeguard interactive latency during NVMe pressure.
- Evaluate hooking model outputs into a lightweight rule engine to surface deterministic customs flags (so operators see a deterministic baseline + model suggestions).

End of notebook entry.
